correctness.rationale: The time-jq observation rows of one fixed Rule 60 site correspond to 1,H,H²,... in F2[X]/(X^n-1) for H=(1+X)^q; row rank is the degree of the minimal polynomial of H, with initial powers independent. Over F_(2^r), X^n-1 splits into m=2^r-1 distinct mth roots, each of local thickness 2^a. The root at X=1 yields nilpotent exponent ceil(2^a/q), whereas each other root has leading nonzero w^(2^b) term, exponent 2^max(a-b,0); power-map collisions on F_(2^r)^× number h=m-1 if gcd(u,m)=1, otherwise m/gcd(u,m). Their LCM yields R=ceil(2^a/q)+2^max(a-b,0)h for all r>=2,a>=0,q>=1. Comparison with n proves perfect recovery iff (a=0 and gcd(q,m)=1) or (a>=1 and q=1). Independently computed actual bit rows and Gaussian-eliminated ranks for 570 parameter triples, all matching, without inferring infinity from those tests.
